title: Exploring Local Phonon Behavior on Oxide Nanoparticle Surfaces
content: Phonon behavior at surfaces may play a key role in facilitating thermochemical reactions taking place on nanoparticle catalysts. Understanding the role that phonons play on a reaction is not well understood in part because of a lack of high spatial resolution experimental explorations of phonon behaviors near the nanoparticle surfaces. Traditional surface science methods used for phonon detection, e.g., high-resolution electron energy-loss spectroscopy (HREELS) and He atom scattering (HAS), can only be applied to relatively large and clean surfaces [1], and are not suitable for detecting behavior on nanoparticle surfaces, which usually have sizes less than 50nm with different facets, edges and non-periodic defects, e.g., steps. With the development of monochromated EELS, probing the local phonon density of states with high spatial and energy resolution in a scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) is now feasible [2]. With a careful selection of parameters, some information about momentum transfer can be achieved, while still maintaining sufficient spatial and energy resolution [3]. Combined with our novel neural network denoiser, here we demonstrate a case studying local phonon behavior on NiO nanoparticles.
